facets.answer: NVIDIA reported shipping initial Vera Rubin samples to customers. Management has guided to production shipments beginning in the second half of 2026, starting in Q3, and has said the platform is already in production; Wistron is preparing to produce the Superchip. These support progress and manufacturing readiness, but do not confirm that commercial-volume customer shipments have begun or establish shipment scale. Supply-chain constraints are a potential risk to the schedule.

Customer-side validation has occurred: CoreWeave completed bring-up and validation of NVL72. That is a technical milestone, not proof of routine production service or widespread deployment. Announced Vera Rubin AI-factory projects, including SK Telecom’s first factory planned for 2027 and NAVER’s planned expansion, remain future deployments.

The material does not report realized Vera Rubin revenue. NVIDIA management guided to nearly $20 billion in standalone CPU revenue this year; this is an expectation, not reported revenue, and it is not total revenue for Vera Rubin systems or the platform. The card therefore supports commercial revenue potential, but not material revenue realization to date.
